questions.text: The railway ministry's ______ of the new safety protocol was praised by the standing committee, although the implementation timeline remains uncertain.
questions.solution:
1. The possessive "ministry's" followed by "of" requires a noun (the object of the preposition).
2. "Adopt" is a verb and "adaptive" is an adjective – both syntactically impossible here.
3. Between the two nouns, "adoption" means formal acceptance, while "adaption" means modification; a protocol is adopted, not adapted.
4. Hence the only word fitting both grammar and meaning is "adoption".

questions.text:
Convert the following direct speech into correct indirect speech:

She said, "If I must submit the proposal by tomorrow, I will work overnight."

options.label: A
options.text: She said that if she must submit the proposal by the next day, she will work overnight.

options.label: B
options.text: She said that if she had to submit the proposal by the next day, she would work overnight.

options.label: C
options.text: She said that if she would have to submit the proposal by the next day, she would work overnight.

options.label: D
options.text: She said that if she has to submit the proposal by the next day, she will work overnight.

questions.solution:
1. Reporting verb 'said' is past → backshift tenses.
2. 'must' (modal of obligation) becomes 'had to'.
3. 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'.
4. In the conditional clause, 'will' becomes 'would'.
5. Pronouns: 'I' → 'she'.
Only option B applies all changes correctly.

questions.text: The Indian Railways' new high‑speed corridor project (1) ______ by the Ministry last year. If the environmental clearance (2) ______ on time, the construction (3) ______ by 2027. However, the contractor warned that unless the land acquisition (4) ______ expedited, the deadline would slip. Choose the set of verb forms that correctly fills blanks (1)–(4).

options.label: A
options.text: was approved; is granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: B
options.text: has been approved; is granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: C
options.text: was approved; was granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: D
options.text: was approved; is granted; will be completed; is expedited

questions.solution: 1. ‘last year’ demands past simple passive → was approved. 2. First‑conditional ‘if’ clause uses present simple passive → is granted. 3. Main clause with ‘by 2027’ requires future perfect passive → will have been completed. 4. ‘unless’ clause for a hypothetical future uses present simple passive → is expedited.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and select the sentence in which the connector is used incorrectly, disrupting the logical coherence of the passage.

(1) The Ministry of Railways launched 'Mission Raftaar' to boost the average speed of freight trains across the network.
(2) However, the initiative received unanimous support from all zonal railways.
(3) Moreover, the budget allocation for the project was enhanced by 12% in the supplementary demands.
(4) Consequently, the revised timeline targets completion by March 2026, six months ahead of the original schedule.

options.label: A
options.text: The Ministry of Railways launched 'Mission Raftaar' to boost the average speed of freight trains across the network.

options.label: B
options.text: However, the initiative received unanimous support from all zonal railways.

options.label: C
options.text: Moreover, the budget allocation for the project was enhanced by 12% in the supplementary demands.

options.label: D
options.text: Consequently, the revised timeline targets completion by March 2026, six months ahead of the original schedule.

questions.solution:
1. Identify the connector in each sentence: (1) none, (2) However, (3) Moreover, (4) Consequently.
2. Check logical relation: (1) states launch; (2) says support – no contrast, so 'However' is wrong.
3. (3) adds info – 'Moreover' fits.
4. (4) shows result of budget hike – 'Consequently' fits.
5. Hence sentence (2) contains the inappropriate connector.

questions.text: The 'Digital India' initiative, launched in 2015, aims to transform the country into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy, **by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring government services are made available electronically**. Which of the following replacements for the bold part makes the sentence grammatically correct and stylistically consistent?

options.label: A
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring government services are made available electronically

options.label: B
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and making government services available electronically

options.label: C
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and to ensure government services are made available electronically

options.label: D
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring that government services are made available electronically

questions.solution:
1. The phrase after 'by' contains a list of three actions; parallelism requires all three to be gerund phrases.
2. Original third item 'ensuring government services are made available electronically' is a clause, not a gerund.
3. Option B changes it to 'making government services available electronically' – a gerund matching 'providing' and 'promoting'.
4. Option C introduces infinitive 'to ensure', breaking parallelism.
5. Option D retains clause structure with 'ensuring that...'.
6. Option A is the original erroneous version.
7. Only B maintains parallel gerund structure and formal register.
8. Therefore B is correct.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, the idiom in bold is used incorrectly. Choose the option that best replaces the bold idiom to convey the intended meaning.

After missing the last train, Ravi was **on cloud nine** as he had to walk home in the rain.
questions.solution:
1. The context shows Ravi is unhappy (missed train, walk in rain).
2. "On cloud nine" means extremely happy – opposite of required meaning.
3. Options A, B, D are all positive happiness idioms.
4. Option C "down in the dumps" means sad/dejected, fitting the context.
5. Hence the correct replacement is "down in the dumps".

questions.text: The new Vande Bharat Express, which was inaugurated last month, have reduced the travel time between Delhi and Varanasi by nearly three hours.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the main subject: "The new Vande Bharat Express" (singular).
2. The relative clause "which was inaugurated last month" does not change the number.
3. Singular subject requires singular verb → "has reduced".
4. Other options use plural or wrong tense.

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana aims to provide affordable housing to the urban poor; ______, the implementation has been slowed by land acquisition disputes.
questions.solution:
1. The first clause states a positive aim.
2. The second clause presents a hindrance, showing contrast.
3. 'However' signals contrast; 'therefore', 'consequently' show result; 'moreover' adds information.
4. Only 'however' fits the logical relation.

questions.text: The ______ of the new railway timetable was evident in the reduced waiting time.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence needs a singular noun after "The" and before "of".
2. "Affect" is a verb; "affects" is verb (3rd person singular).
3. "Effects" is a plural noun, but the verb "was" signals a singular subject.
4. "Effect" is a singular noun meaning "result". Hence "effect" fits.

questions.text: The minister's speech was replete with platitudes, yet the audience remained __________.
questions.solution: The sentence says the audience stayed unchanged despite empty talk. 'Indifferent' means showing no interest or concern, fitting the context. 'Apathetic' is close but implies a deeper lack of feeling, often used for persons, not a collective reaction. 'Elated' and 'ecstatic' denote strong positive emotions, opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.text: The railway ministry announced that the new Vande Bharat service ______ the travel time between Lucknow and Varanasi by nearly two hours, a claim that surprised many commuters.
questions.solution:
1. The reporting verb 'announced' is in past tense.
2. In indirect speech, a future tense ('will cut') shifts to 'would cut'.
3. 'cuts' (present) and 'has cut' (present perfect) do not follow the backshift rule.
4. Therefore the correct form is 'would cut'.

questions.text: The new metro line, ______ it was inaugurated amid much fanfare, ______ reduced the average commute time by 15 minutes.
questions.solution:
1. The clause after the first blank must show contrast with the main clause (the line reduced time despite fanfare). "Although" fits; "because" and "since" imply cause, not contrast.
2. The main verb needs present perfect to indicate an effect continuing to present: "has reduced". "Had reduced" is past perfect (requires a past reference), "will have reduced" is future perfect.
3. Only option A satisfies both contrast and correct tense.

questions.text: By the time the new Vande Bharat Express ______ its inaugural run from Delhi to Varanasi, the railway ministry had already completed the safety audit for the entire corridor.
questions.solution:
1. The main clause uses past perfect ('had already completed'), establishing a past reference point.
2. 'By the time' introduces a subordinate clause that denotes an event occurring at that past reference point.
3. The subordinate clause therefore takes the simple past tense.
4. Among the options, only 'started' is simple past.

questions.text: Despite the minister’s assurance that the new policy would not fail to alleviate the farmers’ distress, the opposition claimed it would ______ the situation.
questions.solution:
1. Parse the double negative: "not fail to alleviate" means "will alleviate".
2. The opposition claims the policy would ______ the situation, indicating the opposite effect.
3. The blank therefore requires an antonym of "alleviate".
4. Among the choices, "exacerbate" means to worsen, the direct antonym.
5. "Mitigate", "ameliorate", and "alleviate" are synonyms of alleviate.
6. Hence the correct fill is "exacerbate".

questions.text:
Select the option that best improves the following sentence:

"If the committee would have been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence."

options.label: A
options.text: Had the committee been more vigilant, the proposal would have been approved without any delay, and the members would have been commended for their diligence.

options.label: B
options.text: If the committee had been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would have been commended for their diligence.

options.label: C
options.text: Had the committee been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence.

options.label: D
options.text: If the committee would have been more vigilant, the proposal would have been approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence.

questions.solution: 1. The if‑clause must use past perfect (had been), not "would have been". 2. The main clause requires perfect modal "would have been approved" to match the counter‑factual past. 3. The second coordinate clause must keep the same perfect modal "would have been commended" for parallelism. 4. Only option A satisfies all three rules.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, one part is underlined. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part without changing the meaning of the sentence.

"The committee members, **in spite of the fact that they had very limited time**, managed to finalize the report before the deadline."

Which of the following is the most suitable replacement?

options.label: A
options.text: A. although they were pressed for time

options.label: B
options.text: B. even though they were short of time

options.label: C
options.text: C. despite having a tight schedule

options.label: D
options.text: D. while they were short of time

questions.solution: The original phrase means ‘although they had limited time’. Option C conveys the same meaning concisely: ‘despite having a tight schedule’. Options A and B use ‘although/even though’ which are correct but change the structure and make the sentence slightly wordy; option D uses ‘while’, which suggests simultaneity rather than concession. Hence C is the best fit.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, the underlined segment contains an error. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct.

The farmer, **despite of his best efforts**, could not harvest the crop on time.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the error: "despite of" is incorrect; "despite" is a preposition that does not take "of".
2. The correct phrase is "despite his best efforts".
3. Option A matches this correction.
4. Option B repeats the error.
5. Option C omits required "of" after "in spite".
6. Option D changes meaning and structure.
7. Therefore, Option A is the only grammatically correct replacement.

questions.text: The ______ of the new policy was evident when the manager decided to ______ the outdated procedure.
questions.solution:
1. Identify that both blanks require the same word.
2. First blank needs a noun meaning "process of improving".
3. Second blank needs a verb meaning "to improve thoroughly".
4. "Overhaul" functions as both noun and verb with that sense.
5. Other options are only noun (revision, amendment, modification) or verb only (amend).

questions.text: The government launched the 'Digital Village' scheme to provide high-speed internet to rural areas. ______, many villages still lack reliable electricity, limiting the scheme's impact.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the logical relation between the two sentences.
2. First sentence states a positive initiative; second sentence states a persisting problem that hinders it.
3. This is a contrast, not cause-effect, addition, or result.
4. Choose the connector that signals contrast: 'However'.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, the underlined segment is shown in brackets. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

The board [gave the nod to] the merger proposal.
questions.solution:
The idiom "gave the nod to" means "approved" and is followed by an object without a preposition.
The underlined segment includes the preposition "to", so the replacement must be a transitive verb in the same tense (simple past).
"approved" fits directly: "The board approved the merger proposal."
"approved the merger proposal" repeats the object, making the sentence redundant.
"nodded" and "gave approval" either change meaning or retain the incorrect preposition.

questions.text: The state government launched the 'Green Corridor' initiative to plant ten lakh saplings along the national highways. ______, the forest department reported a 12% increase in survival rate compared to the previous drive. Environmentalists welcomed the move, urging stricter monitoring of illegal logging.
questions.solution:
1. The first sentence announces a new tree‑planting drive.
2. The second sentence states a positive outcome (12% higher survival).
3. The logical link is cause‑effect/result.
4. "Consequently" signals result; "However" signals contrast; "Moreover" adds info; "Nevertheless" concedes.
5. Only "Consequently" fits the cause‑effect relation.

questions.text: The railway board, which was constituted in 2022, have been monitoring the punctuality of trains since the new timetable was implemented, and it are yet to release its findings. Which of the following rectifies all the errors in the sentence?

options.label: A
options.text: The railway board, which was constituted in 2022, has been monitoring the punctuality of trains since the new timetable was implemented, and it is yet to release its findings.

options.label: B
options.text: The railway board, which was constituted in 2022, have been monitoring the punctuality of trains since the new timetable was implemented, and it is yet to release its findings.

options.label: C
options.text: The railway board, which was constituted in 2022, has been monitoring the punctuality of trains since the new timetable was implemented, and they are yet to release their findings.

options.label: D
options.text: The railway board, which was constituted in 2022, has been monitoring the punctuality of trains since the new timetable had been implemented, and it is yet to release its findings.

questions.solution: 1. Collective noun ‘board’ takes singular verb → ‘has been’ (not ‘have been’). 2. Pronoun ‘it’ requires singular verb → ‘is’ (not ‘are’). 3. Option A corrects both; B leaves first error; C changes number of board; D adds unnecessary past‑perfect.

questions.text: The committee did not praise the proposal for its innovation; ______, the budget constraints forced them to reject it.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the logical relation between the two clauses.
2. First clause is negative ("did not praise") – it states a lack of praise.
3. Second clause adds another negative factor (budget constraints) – it supplements, not contrasts.
4. Hence an additive connector like "moreover" fits; contrast or cause‑effect connectors are wrong.

questions.text: The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationary supplies in the platform. Choose the option that corrects both the homophone and the preposition errors.

options.label: A
options.text: The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationery supplies in the platform.

options.label: B
options.text: The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationary supplies on the platform.

options.label: C
options.text: The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationary supplies at the platform.

options.label: D
options.text: The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationery supplies on the platform.

questions.solution:
1. Spot the homophone error: 'stationary' (not moving) should be 'stationery' (writing materials).
2. Spot the preposition error: 'in the platform' is incorrect for placing items; the correct preposition is 'on the platform'.
3. Apply both corrections to get: 'The station master asked the clerk to keep the stationery supplies on the platform.'
4. Match with options – only option D has both corrections.

questions.text: The Ministry of Railways launched the 'Green Track' initiative in 2023 to reduce carbon emissions. Since its inception, the programme (1) ______ a 12% drop in fuel consumption, (2) ______ the target of 15% remains unmet.
questions.solution:
1. The phrase 'Since its inception' requires present perfect tense → 'has achieved'.
2. The first clause states a positive result; the second clause says the target is still unmet → contrast.
3. Among connectors, only 'yet' expresses contrast appropriately with a comma.
4. Option A matches both tense and logic; others fail either tense or logical relation.

questions.text:
Choose the option that correctly rectifies all errors in the following sentence:

The railway ministry, which have been planning the new high-speed corridor since 2022, are yet to acquire the land, however the budget allocation was approved last month.

options.label: A
options.text: The railway ministry, which has been planning the new high-speed corridor since 2022, is yet to acquire the land, but the budget allocation was approved last month.

options.label: B
options.text: The railway ministry, which have been planning the new high-speed corridor since 2022, is yet to acquire the land, but the budget allocation was approved last month.

options.label: C
options.text: The railway ministry, which has been planning the new high-speed corridor since 2022, are yet to acquire the land, but the budget allocation was approved last month.

options.label: D
options.text: The railway ministry, which has been planning the new high-speed corridor since 2022, is yet to acquire the land, however the budget allocation was approved last month.

questions.solution:
1. Subject "The railway ministry" is singular → verbs must be singular.
2. "have been" → "has been".
3. "are yet to acquire" → "is yet to acquire".
4. "however" as a conjunction without semicolon is wrong; use coordinating conjunction "but".
5. Only option A applies all three corrections.

questions.text:
Definition: A specialist who investigates the historical development and origin of words.

Sentence: The ______ traced the entry of the word 'juggernaut' into English from the Odia term 'Jagannātha'.

Choose the word that satisfies both the definition and the sentence.
questions.solution:
1. The definition describes the study of word origins — etymology.
2. The practitioner of etymology is an etymologist.
3. Philologist studies language broadly, not specifically origins.
4. Lexicographer compiles dictionaries; linguist analyses language structure.
5. Only 'etymologist' fits both the definition and the sentence context.

questions.text: The railway ministry's new digital ticketing system was designed to ______ the long queues at counters, yet the staff, not only failed to adopt the technology but also ______ the confusion among passengers.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the correlative conjunction "not only ... but also" linking two actions of the staff.
2. The first blank follows "designed to" requiring an infinitive verb expressing the system's positive aim.
3. The context "long queues" suggests a verb like eliminate/reduce/alleviate; "increase" is opposite.
4. The second blank follows "but also" and must be a past-tense verb parallel to "failed".
5. The staff's failure to adopt technology would worsen confusion, so the verb must be negative (exacerbated/intensified).
6. "Mitigated" and "resolved" are positive, contradicting the logic.
7. Only option A pairs a positive aim (eliminate) with a negative outcome (exacerbated).
8. Hence, "eliminate, exacerbated" is the correct choice.

questions.text: Had the ‘Green Track’ initiative not ______ the targeted emission cuts, the ministry would have revised its carbon‑credit strategy.
questions.solution:
1. The clause uses past‑perfect conditional: "Had … not + past participle".
2. Only past participles fit: "affected" and "effected".
3. "Affected" = influenced; "effected" = brought about/ caused.
4. The initiative’s purpose is to *cause* the cuts, so "effected" is semantically correct.
5. Base forms "affect" / "effect" are not past participles.

questions.text: The RBI panel ______ the proposal, citing insufficient data.
questions.solution: The phrase "citing insufficient data" gives a negative justification; therefore the panel would not approve, defer, or amend the proposal positively — it would reject it.

questions.text: The committee decided to postpone the meeting, ______ the members had not received the agenda.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the logical relation: the postponement is caused by the members not receiving the agenda.
2. The connector must express cause.
3. "because" shows cause; "although" shows contrast, "unless" shows condition, "while" shows time.
4. Only "because" fits the cause‑effect structure.

questions.text: A person who studies the origin and history of words is called a ____.
questions.solution:
1. The definition describes the study of word origins → etymology.
2. The practitioner of etymology is an etymologist.
3. Entomologist studies insects, epidemiologist studies diseases, ethnologist studies cultures – all unrelated.
4. Hence the only word matching the definition is etymologist.

questions.text: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence: The bank manager asked the clerk to ____ the revised guidelines before the audit.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence needs a verb meaning 'to receive willingly'.
2. 'Accept' fits this meaning.
3. 'Except' is a preposition meaning 'excluding'.
4. 'Expect' means 'to anticipate'.
5. 'Aspect' is a noun meaning 'a facet'.
6. Therefore, 'accept' is the only appropriate choice.

questions.text: Despite the government's announcement of a new subsidy for small farmers, ______ the allocation was delayed due to procedural hurdles; ______ the intended beneficiaries received the aid only after the harvest season.
questions.solution:
1. The opening "Despite" sets up a contrast, so the first blank needs a contrast connector (however/nevertheless).
2. The semicolon links two independent clauses; the second blank must show the result of the delay (consequently/as a result).
3. Only option A supplies a contrast word followed by a result word.
4. Options B, C, D either add information, repeat contrast, or reverse the logic.

questions.text: The newly launched Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi have reduced the travel time to eight hours, and they are expected to boost tourism in the region. Choose the grammatically correct version:

options.label: A
options.text: The newly launched Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi has reduced the travel time to eight hours, and it is expected to boost tourism in the region.

options.label: B
options.text: The newly launched Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi have reduced the travel time to eight hours, and it is expected to boost tourism in the region.

options.label: C
options.text: The newly launched Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi has reduced the travel time to eight hours, and they are expected to boost tourism in the region.

options.label: D
options.text: The newly launched Vande Bharat Express between Delhi and Varanasi have reduced the travel time to eight hours, and they are expected to boost tourism in the region.

questions.solution:
1. Subject 'Vande Bharat Express' is singular → verb must be 'has reduced', not 'have reduced'.
2. Pronoun referring to the singular subject must be 'it', not 'they'.
3. Only option A corrects both errors; B fails subject‑verb, C fails pronoun, D has both errors.

questions.text: The Union Government launched the ‘Kisan Samridhi Yojana’ during the ______ festival, targeting a twofold rise in the earnings of marginal farmers by 2027.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the scheme as agricultural, aimed at farmers.
2. Agricultural schemes in India are traditionally announced during harvest festivals.
3. Pongal is a major harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, closely linked to farming.
4. Diwali, Holi, and Eid are not harvest festivals.
5. Therefore the blank must be filled with the harvest festival name: Pongal.

questions.text:
Identify the part of the following sentence that contains a grammatical error:

If the railway board would have approved the tender earlier, the project could be launched without any further delay.

options.label: A
options.text: If the railway board would have approved the tender earlier

questions.solution:
1. The sentence is a third conditional (unreal past).
2. Correct form: If + past perfect (had approved), ... would/could have + past participle.
3. The if‑clause uses "would have approved" instead of "had approved".
4. Hence the error lies in the first segment.

questions.text: The ministry's decision to ______ the subsidy for electric vehicles was praised, yet the simultaneous move to ______ the tax rebate for hybrid models drew criticism.
questions.solution:
1. The conjunction "yet" signals a contrast between the two actions.
2. First blank needs a verb meaning increase (positive) to match "praised".
3. Second blank needs a verb meaning decrease (negative) to match "criticism".
4. Check each pair for opposite polarity and proper collocation with "subsidy" and "rebate".
5. Only "augment" (increase) and "curtail" (reduce) satisfy both conditions.
6. Other options either share the same polarity or use verbs that do not collocate naturally.
7. Hence the correct choice is "augment, curtail".

questions.text: The railway board did not sanction the new line ______ the environmental clearance was obtained.
questions.solution:
1. Main clause is negative ('did not sanction').
2. Negative main clause + time clause requires 'until' to show action not happening up to a point.
3. 'Unless' introduces a condition, not a time limit.
4. 'Because' gives a reason, illogical with negative.
5. 'Although' shows contrast, not the intended temporal sequence.

questions.text: The ministry's clarification stated that the new directive does not ______ the existing provisions of the Act.
questions.solution:
1. Spot the confusing pair: affect (verb = influence) vs. effect (verb = bring about).
2. The clause “does not ______” needs a verb meaning “influence”.
3. “Affect” fits: the directive does not influence the provisions.
4. “Effect” would mean “does not bring about the provisions” – illogical.
5. “Amend” and “override” are not the tested confusing pair.
→ Correct choice: affect.

questions.text: Indian Railways launched the 'Mission Raftaar' in 2017 to increase average speeds on major corridors. By 2020, the dedicated freight corridors had reduced transit time by 30%, and the introduction of semi‑high‑speed trainsets had cut journey durations on the Delhi‑Howrah route by nearly two hours. __________. Consequently, the ministry announced a fresh capital outlay of ₹1.2 lakh crore for the next five years to upgrade signalling and track infrastructure.

options.label: A
options.text: Moreover, the upgrades have already attracted private investment, reducing the fiscal burden on the exchequer.

options.label: B
options.text: Nevertheless, the upgrades have not fully addressed the chronic congestion on the Mughalsarai‑Patna stretch.

options.label: C
options.text: These gains, however, underscored the pressing requirement for additional rolling stock and modern signalling.

options.label: D
options.text: Thus, the upgrades have eliminated all delays, making further investment unnecessary.

questions.solution: 1. The paragraph narrates past achievements (past perfect). 2. The sentence after the blank starts with "Consequently", so the blank must provide a cause in past tense. 3. Option C uses past tense "underscored" and a concessive "however" that logically leads to a consequence. 4. Options A and B use present perfect, breaking tense consistency. 5. Option D contradicts the following announcement and misuses "Thus" with "Consequently".

questions.text: The railway ministry introduced a revised timetable for all express trains; ______, the number of passenger complaints regarding delays dropped by 35% in the following quarter.
questions.solution:
1. First clause: action (revised timetable).
2. Second clause: positive outcome (complaints dropped).
3. Blank requires a result connector.
4. "Consequently" shows result.
5. "However" = contrast, "meanwhile" = time, "moreover" = addition.
6. Only "consequently" fits logically.

questions.text: The railway board decided to revise the ______ for the summer special trains.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence discusses changing the ticket price for summer special trains.
2. The term for ticket price in railway context is "fare".
3. "Fair" means just or an exhibition; "fear" is an emotion; "far" indicates distance.
4. Only "fare" fits the meaning.
5. Therefore the correct option is "fare".

questions.text: The government's new insurance scheme **mitigates** the financial impact of natural disasters on farmers.
questions.solution:
1. 'Mitigates' means to make something less severe or painful.
2. 'Alleviates' carries the same sense of lessening severity without removing it entirely.
3. 'Reduces' is broader and can imply a quantitative cut, not specifically severity.
4. 'Eliminates' and 'prevents' imply total removal or avoidance, which overstates the meaning.
5. Hence the best synonym in context is 'alleviates'.

questions.text: The state government's new health scheme was **not unviable**; it only required better outreach. Choose the word opposite in meaning to the highlighted word.
questions.solution: 1. Highlighted word is "unviable". 2. Its antonym is formed by removing the negative prefix "un-" → "viable". 3. The preceding "not" does not alter the target word for antonym selection. 4. Among the options, only "viable" is the direct antonym; the others are synonyms or unrelated.

questions.text: The new agricultural scheme aims to boost farmers' income ______ it ______ sustainable water usage.
questions.solution:
1. The subject "scheme" performs two actions: "aims to boost" and a second action.
2. To add a second action without contrast, use the coordinating conjunction "and".
3. The second verb must be in the same tense as "aims" (present simple), so "ensures" is required.
4. Options with "but", "while", "whereas" introduce contrast; "ensuring" and "ensured" break parallelism.

questions.text: Despite the team's initial optimism, the project ______ when the funding was abruptly withdrawn.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence sets a contrast: initial optimism vs. outcome after funding loss.
2. The blank needs an idiom meaning "failed completely".
3. "hit the roof" = became very angry; "broke the ice" = initiated conversation; "turned a corner" = started improving.
4. Only "went belly up" means "collapsed/failed".
5. Hence the correct fill is "went belly up".

questions.text: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.

options.label: A
options.text: The newly launched Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, which aims to provide direct income support to small farmers, have been praised for its timely disbursement since the last fiscal year.

options.label: B
options.text: The newly launched Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, which aims to provide direct income support to small farmers, has been praised for its timely disbursement from the last fiscal year.

options.label: C
options.text: The newly launched Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, which aims to provide direct income support to small farmers, has been praised for its timely disbursement since the last fiscal year.

options.label: D
options.text: The newly launched Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, which aim to provide direct income support to small farmers, has been praised for its timely disbursement since the last fiscal year.

questions.solution:
1. Subject is the singular noun "scheme" → verb must be singular "has been".
2. Relative pronoun "which" refers to "scheme" → verb "aims" (singular).
3. "Since" denotes a point in time; "from" is incorrect here.
4. Option C meets all three rules; A, B, D each violate at least one.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate replacement for the underlined segment in the following sentence:

If the new freight corridor **had been completed** by March, the logistics cost will have reduced significantly.
questions.solution:
1. Main clause uses future perfect "will have reduced".
2. A real future condition requires present perfect in the if‑clause.
3. "had been completed" is past perfect (third conditional).
4. "is completed" lacks perfect aspect.
5. "will be completed" shifts tense to future.
6. Only "has been completed" provides the required present perfect.
7. Therefore option B is correct.

questions.text: Select the sentence that correctly uses the subjunctive mood after ‘essential that’, maintains subject‑verb agreement with the collective noun ‘team’, and keeps tense consistency throughout.

options.label: A
options.text: It is essential that the project be completed on time, and the team ensures that all safety norms are followed.

options.label: B
options.text: It is essential that the project is completed on time, and the team ensures that all safety norms are followed.

options.label: C
options.text: It is essential that the project be completed on time, and the team ensure that all safety norms are followed.

options.label: D
options.text: It is essential that the project be completed on time, and the team ensures that all safety norms were followed.

questions.solution:
1. Subjunctive after ‘essential that’ requires base form ‘be completed’ – eliminates option B.
2. Collective noun ‘team’ takes singular verb ‘ensures’ – eliminates option C.
3. Tense consistency: main clause present (‘is essential’) → subordinate verbs present (‘ensures’, ‘are followed’) – eliminates option D (uses past ‘were followed’).
4. Only option A satisfies all three criteria.

questions.text:
The following sentence contains three grammatical errors. Choose the option that corrects all of them.

"The newly introduced 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, which aim to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries, have been delayed due to lack of coordination, and the government is considering to revise the framework."

options.label: A
options.text: The newly introduced 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, which aims to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries, has been delayed due to lack of coordination, and the government is considering revising the framework.

options.label: B
options.text: The newly introduced 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, which aim to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries, has been delayed due to lack of coordination, and the government is considering revising the framework.

options.label: C
options.text: The newly introduced 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, which aims to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries, have been delayed due to lack of coordination, and the government is considering revising the framework.

options.label: D
options.text: The newly introduced 'PM Gati Shakti' scheme, which aims to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries, has been delayed due to lack of coordination, and the government is considering to revise the framework.

questions.solution:
1. Subject‑verb agreement: ‘scheme’ is singular → ‘which aims’, ‘has been delayed’.
2. After ‘considering’ use gerund → ‘considering revising’.
3. Only option A applies all three corrections.

questions.text: The revised GST amendment is not expected to ______ the compliance burden on micro‑enterprises.
questions.solution:
1. The infinitive "to" demands the base form of the verb → discard "affects" and "effects".
2. "Effect" as a verb means "bring about"; "not expected to bring about the compliance burden" is illogical.
3. "Affect" means "influence"; "not expected to influence the compliance burden" fits the context.
4. Therefore the only grammatically and semantically correct choice is "affect".

questions.text: The proposed high‑speed rail corridor, ______ constructed on a dedicated alignment, is expected to halve the journey time between the two metros.
questions.solution:
1. The blank introduces a reduced adverbial clause with the past participle "constructed".
2. Only "when" (or "once") can directly precede a past participle to form a reduced time clause.
3. "While" requires a present participle ("while constructing") or a full finite clause.
4. "Although" and "whereas" demand a complete clause with subject and verb.
5. Hence "when" is the sole grammatically correct connector.

questions.text: Had the rural broadband rollout been completed on schedule, the digital literacy targets would have been achieved; ______, the persistent delays have left 38 % of villages without connectivity.
questions.solution: 1. The opening clause uses the past‑unreal conditional "Had … been completed … would have been achieved", signalling a hypothetical situation contrary to fact. 2. The second clause states the actual outcome of the real‑world delays. 3. The logical link is therefore result/cause‑effect, not contrast or addition. 4. Among the choices, only "consequently" functions as a conjunctive adverb expressing result.

questions.text: The new railway minister ______ the long‑standing issue of delayed freight trains by introducing a real‑time tracking system.

options.label: A
options.text: hit the nail on the head

options.label: C
options.text: let the cat out of the bag

options.label: D
options.text: took the bull by the horns

questions.solution:
1. Identify the meaning needed: confront and solve a difficult problem directly.
2. Evaluate each idiom:
   - hit the nail on the head = identify correctly, not solve.
   - burned the midnight oil = work late, unrelated.
   - let the cat out of the bag = reveal a secret.
   - took the bull by the horns = tackle a problem head‑on.
3. Only option D matches the required sense.

questions.text: The board decided to ______ the issue to rest after the heated debate.
questions.solution: 1. The phrase "to ______ the issue to rest" requires a bare infinitive after "to". 2. The idiom is "lay something to rest" (transitive verb "lay" + object). 3. "Lie" is intransitive and cannot take an object. 4. "Laying" and "lying" are gerunds, not infinitives. Hence only "lay" satisfies both the idiom and the grammatical form.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows:

"During the annual 'Kite Festival' in the coastal town of Vashapur, the sky was dotted with a myriad of colorful kites. While most participants were jubilant, a few spectators remained **sullen** as they watched their friends soar higher. The organizers, noticing the mood, distributed complimentary sweets to lift the spirits of the onlookers."

In the above passage, the word **sullen** most nearly means:
questions.solution: The context shows spectators were not happy; the organizers tried to lift their spirits. 'Sullen' therefore implies a gloomy, sulky mood. 'Morose' matches this meaning. 'Ecstatic' and 'exuberant' are opposite, while 'indifferent' suggests lack of feeling, not the sulky attitude described.

questions.text: The new policy not only ______ the procedural delays but also ______ transparency in the approval process.
questions.solution:
1. Subject "The new policy" is singular.
2. Connector "not only ... but also" demands parallel verb forms.
3. Present simple third‑person singular verbs needed: "reduces" and "enhances".
4. Only option A supplies both correct forms.

questions.text:
Choose the option that correctly rewrites the following sentence without any grammatical error:

"The committee, which was formed last year to oversee the implementation of the new health scheme, have not yet submitted its report, nor it has responded to the ministry's queries."

options.label: A
options.text: The committee, which was formed last year to oversee the implementation of the new health scheme, has not yet submitted its report, nor it has responded to the ministry's queries.

options.label: B
options.text: The committee, which was formed last year to oversee the implementation of the new health scheme, have not yet submitted its report, nor has it responded to the ministry's queries.

options.label: C
options.text: The committee, which was formed last year to oversee the implementation of the new health scheme, has not yet submitted their report, nor has it responded to the ministry's queries.

options.label: D
options.text: The committee, which was formed last year to oversee the implementation of the new health scheme, has not yet submitted its report, nor has it responded to the ministry's queries.

questions.solution:
1. Subject ‘committee’ is singular → verb must be ‘has’, not ‘have’.
2. After ‘nor’ an auxiliary precedes the subject → ‘nor has it’, not ‘nor it has’.
3. Pronoun for singular ‘committee’ is ‘its’, not ‘their’.
Only option D satisfies all three rules.

questions.text: The official did not let the cat out of the bag regarding the fund allocation, ______ the media still speculated wildly.
questions.solution:
1. The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret.
2. "Did not let the cat out of the bag" means the official kept the allocation secret.
3. The word "still" in the second clause shows that despite the secrecy, the media speculated.
4. This requires a contrastive connector.
5. Among the options, only "nevertheless" expresses contrast.
6. "Therefore", "moreover", "consequently" indicate result or addition, which are illogical here.
7. Hence the correct connector is "nevertheless".

questions.text: The Indian Railways' new 'One Station One Product' scheme aims to ______ local artisans by providing them a platform at railway stations.
questions.solution: The phrase 'aims to ______ local artisans' requires a verb meaning 'to give power or authority to'. 'Empower' fits this meaning and collocates with 'artisans'. 'Employ' means to hire, 'emulate' means to imitate, and 'envelop' means to wrap. Hence, 'empower' is the correct choice.

questions.text: The new policy will have a positive ______ on the rural economy.
questions.solution:
1. The phrase "a positive" requires a noun.
2. "Effect" is a noun meaning result; "affect" is a verb.
3. "Affects" (verb, 3rd person) and "effected" (past participle verb) are not nouns.
4. Hence the only noun that fits is "effect".

questions.text: The railway recruitment board issued ______ important advice to all candidates regarding the new examination pattern.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the noun after the blank: "advice".
2. "Advice" is an uncountable noun; it never takes "a" or "an".
3. The sentence refers to advice in general, not a specific piece, so "the" is not required.
4. Therefore, no article is needed. The correct choice is "no article".

questions.text: The government’s new ‘Green Energy’ scheme intends to subsidize solar panels, wind turbines, and to set up charging stations, besides ensuring that rural households receive uninterrupted power. Select the best improvement.

options.label: A
options.text: The government’s new ‘Green Energy’ scheme intends to subsidize solar panels, wind turbines, and to set up charging stations, besides ensuring that rural households receive uninterrupted power.

options.label: B
options.text: The government’s new ‘Green Energy’ scheme intends to subsidize solar panels, wind turbines, and set up charging stations, besides ensuring that rural households receive uninterrupted power.

options.label: C
options.text: The government’s new ‘Green Energy’ scheme intends to subsidize solar panels, wind turbines, and to set up charging stations, and ensure that rural households receive uninterrupted power.

options.label: D
options.text: The government’s new ‘Green Energy’ scheme intends to subsidize solar panels and wind turbines, set up charging stations, and ensure that rural households receive uninterrupted power.

questions.solution: 1. Spot two errors: (a) after “intends to” the list mixes a bare infinitive (“subsidize”) with a to‑infinitive (“to set up”) → lack of parallelism. (b) “besides ensuring” is a prepositional phrase, not a coordinate clause; the final aim needs a coordinating conjunction “and ensure”. 2. Option D rewrites the list as three bare infinitives (“subsidize …, set up …, and ensure …”) and replaces “besides ensuring” with “and ensure”, fixing both errors. Options B and C each correct only one error.

questions.text: The newly launched ‘One District One Product’ scheme ______ the successful model of the neighbouring state by offering artisans a dedicated e‑marketplace.
questions.solution: 1. Subject ‘scheme’ is singular → verb must be ‘takes’ (eliminate B). 2. The idiom meaning ‘imitate’ is ‘take a leaf out of’ (not ‘from’ or ‘page’). 3. Only option A has both correct verb form and exact idiom wording.

questions.text:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the following sentence, retaining the adverbial phrase 'by the end of the fiscal year' in its appropriate position:

'The finance ministry must have finalised the budget allocation by the end of the fiscal year.'

options.label: A
options.text: The budget allocation must have been finalised by the finance ministry by the end of the fiscal year.

options.label: B
options.text: The budget allocation must have been finalised by the end of the fiscal year the finance ministry.

options.label: C
options.text: The budget allocation must be finalised by the finance ministry by the end of the fiscal year.

options.label: D
options.text: The budget allocation must have been finalised by the finance ministry at the end of the fiscal year.

questions.solution:
1. Active: Subject = The finance ministry; Verb = must have finalised (modal perfect); Object = the budget allocation; Adverbial = by the end of the fiscal year.
2. Passive subject = the budget allocation.
3. Modal perfect passive = must have been finalised.
4. Agent introduced by 'by' = by the finance ministry.
5. Adverbial placed after agent (standard order) = by the end of the fiscal year.
6. Option A matches all steps; B omits 'by' before agent; C uses 'must be' (wrong tense); D changes 'by' to 'at' altering meaning.

questions.text:
The sentence below is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C), (D). One segment contains a grammatical error. Identify the erroneous segment.

(A) Even though the new policy was announced last month
(B) many employees still unaware of its implications
(C) and the management has not provided any clarification yet
(D) which has led to widespread confusion among the staff

options.label: A
options.text: Even though the new policy was announced last month

options.label: B
options.text: many employees still unaware of its implications

options.label: C
options.text: and the management has not provided any clarification yet

options.label: D
options.text: which has led to widespread confusion among the staff

questions.solution:
1. Segment A: "Even though the new policy was announced last month" – correct subordinate clause.
2. Segment B: "many employees still unaware of its implications" – missing auxiliary verb "are"; should be "many employees are still unaware".
3. Segment C: "and the management has not provided any clarification yet" – correct tense and coordination.
4. Segment D: "which has led to widespread confusion among the staff" – correct relative clause.
5. Only segment B contains a grammatical error.

questions.text:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct and contextually appropriate.

Despite the heavy rains, the construction of the new bridge **has been progressing since last monsoon**, and it is expected to be inaugurated by the end of this year.

options.label: A
options.text: has been progressing since last monsoon

options.label: B
options.text: has progressed since the last monsoon

options.label: C
options.text: had been progressing since last monsoon

questions.solution:
1. The action started in the past and continues to the present → present perfect (has progressed), not present perfect continuous.
2. "Since" requires a specific point in time; "last monsoon" is a period, so the definite article "the" is needed → "since the last monsoon".
3. Option B satisfies both corrections; others retain at least one error.

questions.text: The government’s new agricultural subsidy ______ the farmers’ income; ______ the rural economy has shown signs of revival.
questions.solution:
1. A subsidy provides support, so the verb must be positive → boosted (not reduced).
2. Higher income leads to revival, requiring a cause‑effect connector → consequently (not however/nevertheless/therefore with reduced).
3. Only option A satisfies both semantic and logical constraints.

questions.text: The ______ of the scheme was evident, yet the ______ of its execution could not be overlooked.
questions.solution:
1. Both blanks need nouns that are direct morphological antonyms sharing the same root.
2. Only “advantage” → “disadvantage” uses the prefix “dis‑” on the identical base.
3. The other pairs are semantic antonyms but not formed by a single prefix on the same root.
4. Hence the only pair satisfying the morphological‑antonym rule is “advantage, disadvantage”.

questions.text: In the annual report, the phrase "the company's profit margin expanded by 12%" was replaced with "the company's profit margin ______ by twelve percent". Which word best fits the blank?
questions.solution: 1. Identify the meaning of "expanded" in the original sentence – it means to become larger. 2. The numeric cue "by twelve percent" confirms a positive change. 3. Among options, only "increased" denotes a rise in size/amount. 4. "Contracted", "dwindled", and "narrowed" all imply reduction, opposite of "expanded". Hence option C is correct.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, one word is highlighted. Choose the word that best replaces the highlighted word to convey the opposite meaning.

The train remained *stationary* at the platform for ten minutes.
questions.solution:
1. Highlighted word: stationary (meaning not moving).
2. Antonym required: a word meaning moving.
3. Mobile means able to move – correct antonym.
4. Stationery is a homophone (writing material) – wrong meaning.
5. Still is a synonym (not moving) – not opposite.
6. Stationary repeats the original – no change.

questions.text: After the sudden announcement of the new tax slab, the small traders ______, fearing a drop in their already thin margins.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the meaning required: traders are helpless and abandoned after the announcement.
2. "hit the roof" = become very angry – not helpless.
3. "went the extra mile" = make extra effort – opposite sense.
4. "kept their chin up" = stay cheerful – does not convey abandonment.
5. "were left high and dry" = left in a difficult situation without help – matches context.
6. Hence option C is correct.

questions.text: The government announced a new scheme for small farmers; ______, the implementation has been delayed due to bureaucratic hurdles.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the relationship: the first clause states an announcement, the second clause states a delay — a contrast.
2. 'however' signals contrast; 'therefore' and 'consequently' signal result; 'moreover' adds information.
3. Only 'however' correctly conveys the contrast.

questions.text: The Ministry of Agriculture announced ____ unique initiative to boost millet production in rain‑fed districts.
questions.solution:
1. The blank precedes the noun phrase "unique initiative".
2. "Unique" is pronounced /juːˈniːk/, starting with a consonant sound /j/.
3. Indefinite article "a" is used before consonant sounds.
4. "An" is used before vowel sounds – incorrect here.
5. "The" would imply a specific, already‑known initiative – not intended.
6. Zero article cannot precede a singular countable noun.
7. Therefore the correct article is "a".

questions.text:
Choose the option that best improves the following sentence:

The committee, comprising of experts from various fields, have recommended that the new policy be implemented immediately, and that the budget be allocated accordingly.

options.label: A
options.text: The committee, comprising of experts from various fields, have recommended that the new policy be implemented immediately, and that the budget be allocated accordingly.

options.label: B
options.text: The committee, comprising experts from various fields, have recommended that the new policy be implemented immediately, and that the budget be allocated accordingly.

options.label: C
options.text: The committee, comprising of experts from various fields, has recommended that the new policy be implemented immediately, and that the budget be allocated accordingly.

options.label: D
options.text: The committee, comprising experts from various fields, has recommended that the new policy be implemented immediately, and that the budget be allocated accordingly.

questions.solution:
1. ‘Comprising’ does not take ‘of’; remove ‘of’.
2. ‘Committee’ is a collective singular noun → verb ‘has’ not ‘have’.
3. Only option D corrects both errors.

questions.text: In the official circular, the Director General wrote: "All departments shall **commence** the new compliance audit by 1st July." Choose the word that best replaces the highlighted word without changing the formal tone of the sentence.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the register: the sentence is an official government circular, requiring formal administrative language.
2. Analyse each option:
   - "start" and "begin" are neutral/informal verbs, common in everyday speech.
   - "launch" collocates with products, campaigns, or projects, not with audits.
   - "initiate" is the standard formal verb used in orders, directives, and procedural documents.
3. Therefore, "initiate" preserves the formal tone and correct collocation.

questions.text: The Ministry of Railways announced a new ______ to modernize station amenities; ______, the rollout has been postponed due to funding constraints.
questions.solution:
1. The first blank needs a noun denoting a new plan – ‘initiative’, ‘scheme’, ‘project’, ‘programme’ all fit.
2. The semicolon and the second blank require a connector showing contrast because the rollout is postponed despite the announcement.
3. ‘However’ signals contrast; ‘therefore’, ‘moreover’, ‘consequently’ indicate result or addition, which contradict the meaning.
4. Only the pair ‘initiative; however’ satisfies both lexical fit and logical contrast.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, a part is underlined. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part to make the sentence grammatically correct.

The committee, which comprises of senior officials from various ministries, have decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy until the next fiscal year.

options.label: A
options.text: which comprises senior officials from various ministries, has decided

options.label: B
options.text: which comprise senior officials from various ministries, have decided

options.label: C
options.text: comprising senior officials from various ministries, have decided

options.label: D
options.text: comprising of senior officials from various ministries, have decided

questions.solution:
1. ‘Committee’ is a collective noun acting as a unit → singular verb ‘has decided’.
2. ‘Comprises’ never takes ‘of’; correct form is ‘comprises senior officials’.
3. Relative pronoun ‘which’ refers to ‘committee’ (singular) → verb in relative clause ‘comprises’.
4. Option A fixes both errors; B, C, D retain plural verb or wrong preposition.

questions.text:
Identify the part that contains an error in the following sentence:

The new scheme aims to (A) provide financial assistance, (B) ensuring timely disbursement, (C) and to monitor the progress of beneficiaries, (D) which will enhance transparency.
questions.solution:
1. After "aims to" the list must use parallel infinitives: "provide" (to implied) and "to monitor" are infinitives; "ensuring" is a gerund → breaks parallelism → error in (B).
2. (A) "provide financial assistance" correctly follows "aims to".
3. (C) "and to monitor the progress of beneficiaries" maintains infinitive parallelism.
4. (D) "which will enhance transparency" correctly refers to the whole scheme.
5. Distractors: (A) may tempt subject‑verb agreement error; (C) may tempt omission of "to"; (D) may tempt ambiguous antecedent.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, identify the option that correctly rectifies all grammatical errors while preserving the formal tone of an official press release.

"The Ministry of Agriculture have announced that the new subsidy scheme will be launched from 1st April, and it would benefit small farmers across the country, provided they submits the required documents before the deadline."

options.label: A
options.text: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced that the new subsidy scheme will be launched on 1 April and will benefit small farmers across the country, provided they submit the required documents before the deadline.

options.label: B
options.text: The Ministry of Agriculture have announced that the new subsidy scheme will be launched on 1 April and will benefit small farmers across the country, provided they submit the required documents before the deadline.

options.label: C
options.text: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced that the new subsidy scheme would be launched on 1 April and would benefit small farmers across the country, provided they submit the required documents before the deadline.

options.label: D
options.text: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced that the new subsidy scheme will be launched on 1 April and will benefit small farmers across the country, provided they submits the required documents before the deadline.

questions.solution: 1. Subject‑verb: "Ministry" is singular → "has announced". 2. Preposition for a specific date → "on 1 April". 3. Future certainty in formal release → "will be launched" and "will benefit". 4. Conditional clause "provided they" takes plural verb → "submit". Only option A satisfies all four corrections.

questions.text: The Ministry of Railways launched the ‘Station Swachhata Abhiyan’ last month, earmarking ₹1,200 crore for the initial phase. ______. Consequently, the project monitoring committee has mandated weekly progress reports from each zonal contractor. Choose the sentence that best completes the paragraph.

options.label: A
options.text: The ministry stipulated that funds would be released only after verification of milestone completion.

options.label: B
options.text: However, the zonal offices have already reported a 15% cost overrun due to unforeseen geological surveys.

options.label: C
options.text: Therefore, the ministry has decided to postpone the launch ceremony until the next fiscal year.

options.label: D
options.text: Meanwhile, the railway board has approved an additional ₹300 crore for emergency repairs.

questions.solution:
1. The paragraph sets a past context: scheme launched, funds earmarked.
2. The word "Consequently" after the blank signals that the blank must provide a cause for the committee's action.
3. Option A states a condition for fund release (milestone verification), which directly necessitates weekly progress monitoring.
4. Option B opens with "However", a contrast marker, clashing with the following "Consequently".
5. Option C uses "Therefore" suggesting a result of the first sentence, but postponing the ceremony does not trigger monitoring.
6. Option D uses "Meanwhile" indicating simultaneity, not causation.
7. Only Option A supplies a logical cause, maintains past tense, and aligns with the committee's mandate.
8. Hence, Option A is the correct completion.

questions.text:
Four sentences (A)–(D) are given below. Each may contain a subtle grammatical error, but the logical flow of the paragraph is unaffected. Choose the sequence that arranges them into a coherent paragraph.

(A) Indian Railways announced a massive station redevelopment plan for the northern zone last year.
(B) The project, which was sanctioned in March, have already commenced the groundwork.
(C) Upon completion, the station will boast a solar-powered canopy, an automated ticketing system, and a dedicated freight corridor.
(D) The first phase, covering platform extension and canopy installation, is slated to finish by December 2026.
questions.solution:
1. Logical flow: announcement → sanction & commencement → phase deadline → final features.
2. (A) announces the plan.
3. (B) mentions sanction in March and groundwork started (follows announcement).
4. (D) gives first‑phase completion target (follows commencement).
5. (C) describes facilities upon full completion (final).
6. Only sequence A‑B‑D‑C matches this chronology.
7. The subject‑verb error in (B) ("have" → "has") does not alter the order.
8. Hence correct option is A B D C.

questions.text:
Identify the option that corrects all grammatical and stylistic errors in the following sentence while preserving its intended meaning:

"The committee, comprising of senior officials, have decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy, albeit they acknowledge the urgent need for reform."

options.label: A
options.text: The committee, comprising senior officials, has decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy, although they acknowledge the urgent need for reform.

options.label: B
options.text: The committee, composed of senior officials, have decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy, albeit they acknowledge the urgent need for reform.

options.label: C
options.text: The committee, comprising senior officials, has decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy, albeit they acknowledges the urgent need for reform.

options.label: D
options.text: The committee, comprising of senior officials, has decided to postpone the implementation of the new policy, though they acknowledge the urgent need for reform.

questions.solution:
1. 'Committee' is singular → verb must be 'has decided' (not 'have').
2. 'Comprising' does not take 'of' → correct form 'comprising senior officials'.
3. The concessive connector 'albeit they acknowledge' is non‑standard; formal writing prefers 'although they acknowledge'.
4. Only Option A incorporates all three corrections.

questions.text: The newly appointed project manager, Ms. Rao, addressed the team: 'We have secured the funding; ______, the timeline remains tight because the vendor delayed the prototype delivery.' Choose the option that best completes the sentence with a connector that conveys the correct logical relationship, maintains a formal business register, and uses an idiom appropriate for the context.

options.label: A
options.text: however, the onus is on us

options.label: B
options.text: nevertheless, the ball is in our court

options.label: C
options.text: consequently, the onus is on us

options.label: D
options.text: moreover, the ball is in our court

questions.solution:
1. The first clause states funding is secured; the second says timeline stays tight due to vendor delay → a contrast relation is needed.
2. Contrast connectors: "however" or "nevertheless" (both formal).
3. The idiom must express that responsibility now lies with the team in a formal tone → "the onus is on us" (formal) vs. "the ball is in our court" (informal).
4. Only option A combines a contrast connector (however) with a formal responsibility idiom.

questions.text: The administrative department placed an order for new ______ to replenish the office supplies.
questions.solution:
1. The blank needs a noun meaning writing materials (paper, pens).
2. 'Stationery' is the correct noun for office supplies.
3. 'Stationary' means not moving – wrong meaning.
4. 'Stagnant' means not flowing – unrelated.
5. 'Stagnate' is a verb – cannot fit the noun slot.

questions.text: The manager decided to ______ the issue until the next meeting.
questions.solution: The context requires a verb meaning 'postpone'. 'Put off' means to delay. 'Put out' means extinguish, 'put up' means tolerate, 'put down' means suppress. Only 'put off' fits.

questions.text: The station master ______ the delay and ______ the passengers with a polite announcement.
questions.solution:
1. The first blank needs a verb meaning ‘to accept/admit’ in a formal railway context → ‘acknowledged’ fits; ‘ignored’, ‘noticed’, ‘recognized’ are either opposite or too weak.
2. The second blank needs a verb meaning ‘to calm/soothe’ matching a polite announcement → ‘assuaged’ fits; ‘aggravated’, ‘annoyed’, ‘irritated’ convey worsening the situation.
3. Only option A supplies a pair that is both semantically correct and maintains formal register throughout.

questions.text: In the report, the auditor described the company's cash‑flow situation as *robust*. Which of the following words is the best antonym for the underlined word as used in this context?
questions.solution: 1. "Robust" in financial context means strong, stable and able to withstand shocks. 2. The opposite should convey weakness or instability. 3. "Fragile" means easily broken or weakened – the direct opposite. 4. "Fluctuating" means varying, not opposite in strength. 5. "Substantial" is a synonym (large, considerable). 6. "Resilient" is a synonym (able to recover). Hence option A is the correct antonym.

questions.text: The new railway policy aims to ______ the process of ticket booking for senior citizens, making it more accessible and less cumbersome.
questions.solution:
1. The clause "making it more accessible and less cumbersome" signals removal of complexity, not just speed.
2. "Streamline" means to make a process more efficient by simplifying.
3. "Accelerate" only implies speed, not simplification.
4. "Complicate" and "prolong" are antonyms of the intended effect.
5. Hence the precise fit is "streamline".

questions.text: The new agricultural subsidy scheme was announced in March; ______, the disbursement of funds to farmers began only in July due to procedural delays.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the logical relationship: the second clause contrasts the early announcement with the late disbursement.
2. A contrast connector is required; "Nevertheless" signals concession/contrast in formal register.
3. "Consequently" and "Henceforth" imply result or future time — incorrect logic.
4. "Moreover" adds information — does not express contrast.
5. Hence only "Nevertheless" fits both logic and register.

questions.text:
Choose the option that best improves the underlined sentence.

Not only the ministry announced a new subsidy for organic farming, but also it failed to allocate sufficient funds for its implementation.

options.label: A
options.text: Not only the ministry announced a new subsidy for organic farming, but also it failed to allocate sufficient funds for its implementation.

options.label: B
options.text: Not only did the ministry announce a new subsidy for organic farming, but it also failed to allocate sufficient funds for its implementation.

options.label: C
options.text: Not only the ministry announced a new subsidy for organic farming, but also failed to allocate sufficient funds for its implementation.

options.label: D
options.text: Not only did the ministry announce a new subsidy for organic farming, but also it failed to allocate sufficient funds for its implementation.

questions.solution:
1. After “Not only” at the start of a clause, subject‑auxiliary inversion is required → “did the ministry announce”.
2. The correlative pair “Not only … but also” demands parallel structure; the second clause must mirror the first → “but it also failed”.
3. Option B satisfies both inversion and parallelism; others miss inversion (A, C) or keep faulty “but also it” (D).

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells a cricket bat with a marked price of ₹5,000. He offers two alternatives: Scheme A: 15% discount followed by a further 10% discount on the reduced price. Scheme B: A single flat discount of x%. To make the final selling price identical in both schemes, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Discount A = 15%. Remaining = 85%.
Discount B = 10%. Remaining = 90%.
Combined Remaining = 85% x 90% = 0.85 x 0.90 = 0.765.
Total Discount = 1 - 0.765 = 0.235.
x = 23.5%.

questions.text: A bank offers a special 'Festival Savings Scheme' where the interest rate for the first year is 5% per annum on the principal. However, the interest earned in the first year is added to the principal at the end of the year. If a customer deposits ₹10,000 and closes the account after exactly one year, what is the total amount received?
questions.solution:
Simple Interest = (P * R * T) / 100.
Substituting values: P = 10000, R = 5%, T = 1 year.
SI = (10000 * 5 * 1) / 100.
SI = 500.
Total Amount = Principal + Interest = 10000 + 500 = 10500.

questions.text: A retailer marks up a commodity by 25% above its cost price. He then offers a discount of x% on this marked price. If the final selling price equals the original cost price plus half of the initial profit he would have made had there been no discount, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 100.
Initial Profit (if no discount) = Marked Price - CP = 125 - 100 = 25.
Half of this initial profit = 25 / 2 = 12.5.
Target Selling Price = CP + Half Initial Profit = 100 + 12.5 = 112.5.
Marked Price (MP) = 125.
Discount Amount = MP - SP = 125 - 112.5 = 12.5.
Discount Percentage (x) = (Discount / MP) * 100 = (12.5 / 125) * 100 = 10%.

questions.text: A suburban train covers a distance of 120 km in 2 hours at its scheduled speed. On the return journey, due to signal disruptions at exactly 5 platforms encountered, the train incurs a fixed 'delay penalty' of 4 minutes for every platform passed. If the train maintains the exact same average speed between these platforms as it did on the outbound journey, how much total time is required for the entire return trip?
questions.solution:
1. Outbound average speed = 120 km / 2 hrs = 60 km/hr.
2. Return journey distance is also 120 km.
3. Ideal time for return trip at 60 km/hr = 120/60 = 2 hours (120 mins).
4. Delay penalty = 4 minutes per platform * 5 platforms = 20 minutes.
5. Total time = Ideal time + Penalty = 120 mins + 20 mins = 140 mins.

questions.text: A fixed deposit scheme offers Simple Interest (SI) calculated on a daily basis. If the interest for one full year is Rs. 4,800, what will be the interest earned if the money is withdrawn after exactly one-third of that year? Assume a non-leap year.
questions.solution: Total annual SI = ₹4,800. Since it is Simple Interest, the rate is constant per unit time. 1/3rd of a year yields 1/3rd of the total annual interest. Calculation: (1/3) * 4,800 = 1,600.

questions.text:
In a government procurement tender for 'Project Yogi', the contractor declares that the total estimated Cost Price (CP) for a batch of uniforms was calculated as 80% of the total Selling Price (SP). If the final SP for the batch was Rs. 240,000, and the actual expenses incurred were: Materials (40% of CP), Labor (35% of CP), and Overheads (25% of CP), what is the amount spent on Overheads? 

**Note:** The 'Materials' expense was found to be under-estimated by Rs. 5,000 in the initial draft, but the question asks for the **calculated** Overhead based on the declared percentages and the given SP.
questions.solution:
1. Calculate Total CP: SP (240,000) * 80% = Rs. 192,000.
2. Identify Overhead component: Given as 25% of CP.
3. Calculate Overhead Amount: 25% of 192,000 = (192,000 / 4) = Rs. 48,000.
4. Note: The under-estimation info is a distractor for the specific question asking for calculated overhead.

questions.text: A retailer marks up a festive gift item by 40% over its cost price to sell it at a premium. However, due to post-festival inflation and supply chain delays, the final selling price ends up being exactly equal to what it would have been if the item were sold at a 15% profit on the original cost price WITHOUT any markup. What is the Cost Price of the item if the Final Selling Price was Rs. 230?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price = x.
Original Selling Price (with 40% markup) = 1.4x.
Alternative Selling Price (with 15% profit) = 1.15x.
The problem states the Final SP equals the Alternative SP, so Final SP = 1.15x.
We are given Final SP = Rs. 230.
Equation: 1.15x = 230.
Calculation: x = 230 / 1.15.
Division: 230 / 1.15 = 200.

questions.text: A trader marks up the Cost Price (CP) of a commodity by 25% to get the Marked Price (MP). He then offers a 10% discount on this MP. If the final Selling Price (SP) is Rs. 270, what is the trader's profit percentage on the CP?

A confectioner sells 'Assorted Box' X (cost ₹220/kg) and 'Premium Box' Y (cost ₹320/kg). To reduce inventory of Y, he mixes 2 kg of X with 1 kg of Y to create 'Box Z'. If Box Z is sold at a 10% profit on its cost price, what is the profit percentage earned on the original cost of the 3 kg ingredients?
questions.solution:
Cost of 2 kg X = 2 x 220 = 440.
Cost of 1 kg Y = 1 x 320 = 320.
Total Cost Price (CP) of 3 kg = 440 + 320 = 760.
Selling Price (SP) of 3 kg = 760 x 1.10 = 836.
Profit = SP - CP = 836 - 760 = 76.
Profit % = (76 / 760) x 100 = 10%.

questions.text: In a government office, there are 5 files of 'Pending Cases' and 3 files of 'Closed Cases'. A junior officer must select exactly two files for review. The rule is: if the first file selected is 'Pending', the second MUST be 'Closed'; if the first is 'Closed', the second can be anything. If the officer picks a 'Pending' file first, what is the probability that the SECOND file selected turns out to be 'Pending' as well?
questions.solution:
Let P1 = Pending, C1 = Closed. Total = 8.
P(Case 1 is P) * P(Case 2 is P | Case 1 is P) = Probability of two P.
The rule states: If 1st is P, 2nd MUST be C.
Therefore, given 1st is P, probability 2nd is P is 0.
Total probability of (P then P) = P(P1)*0 = 0.

He then marks the price at 25% above his cost price. During a 'festival sale', he offers a 'cash discount' of 10% on the marked price. If the retailer declares that his 'net profit percentage' is calculated on the 'final selling price' rather than the cost price, what is his net profit percentage (rounded to the nearest integer)?

A prudent investor splits a total sum of Rs. 20,000 into two parts. Part A is invested at 6% simple interest per annum, and Part B is invested at 8% simple interest per annum. If the combined annual interest earned from both parts is exactly equal to the simple interest on the entire Rs. 20,000 invested at a blended rate of 7% per annum for one year, what is the amount invested at 6%?
questions.solution:
1. Total Sum = Rs. 20,000.
2. Target Interest (Target Rate) = 7% of 20,000 = Rs. 1,400.
3. Let Part A = x (at 6%) and Part B = 20,000 - x (at 8%).
4. Equation: 0.06x + 0.08(20,000 - x) = 1,400.
5. Simplify: 0.06x + 1,600 - 0.08x = 1,400.
6. Rearrange: -0.02x = -200.
7. Solve: x = 200 / 0.02 = 10,000.

questions.text: An Indian Railways employee saves for a new ticket reservation system upgrade by depositing ₹2,000 at the end of each month into a Public Provident Fund (PPF) account. The bank announces an annual compound interest rate of 7.2% compounded annually. Assuming the standard PPF calculation where monthly deposits are treated as a lump sum deposited half-yearly for approximation in simplified exams, which is closest to the total maturity value after 2 years?
questions.solution:
1. Total principal (24 months * 2000) = ₹48,000.
2. Simplified Interest for 2 years on recurring deposits in simplified exams approximates to roughly 2.5% of the principal over the period.
3. Calculation: 48,000 + (48,000 * 0.025) = 48,000 + 1,200 = ₹49,200.
4. Rounding to nearest option gives ₹49,300.

A train crosses a pole in 18 seconds. The train's speed is 72 km/h. If the train's length is increased by 120 meters, how long will it take to cross the pole?
questions.solution: 72 km/h = 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s. In 18 s the train covers its own length: 20 x 18 = 360 m. After adding 120 m the length is 480 m, so time = 480 / 20 = 24 seconds. The other options ignore the correct speed conversion or the added length.

questions.text: A contractor promises to complete a project in 40 days. He employs 60 men. However, due to supply shortages, the work rate of every single man drops by 25% immediately after day 20. If he wants to finish the job exactly on day 40 regardless of this slowdown, how many additional men must he hire at that moment?
questions.solution: Initial plan: 60 men complete work in 40 days. Halfway (day 20), half the total required work is done. Remaining work needs to be done in remaining 20 days. At day 20, efficiency of each man drops by 25% (becomes 75% of original). Let original rate be R. New rate = 0.75R.
